intro: The cuisine that wrote the rulebook for restaurant cooking: butter, cream, wine and patient technique, from Paris bistros to Provençal olive oil country.
flavours: Butter, cream, wine, shallots, thyme, Dijon mustard
hk: Hong Kong has one of Asia's densest French fine-dining scenes, and bistros all over Central and Sheung Wan.

dishes.name: Croissant
dishes.what: Flaky, crescent-shaped breakfast pastry made by folding layers of butter into dough.

dishes.name: Coq au vin
dishes.what: Chicken braised slowly in red wine until tender; a Burgundy classic.

dishes.name: Beef bourguignon
dishes.what: Rich Burgundy beef stew in a dark red-wine sauce.

dishes.name: Ratatouille
dishes.what: Provençal stew of summer vegetables in olive oil.

dishes.name: Bouillabaisse
dishes.what: Marseille fisherman's stew, served with toast and garlicky rouille sauce.

dishes.name: Steak frites
dishes.what: Bistro staple: pan-fried steak with a pile of thin fries, often with béarnaise.

dishes.name: Duck confit
dishes.what: Duck leg cooked in its own fat (that's what confit means) with crisp skin; a south-west speciality.

dishes.name: Escargots
dishes.what: Snails baked in their shells with sizzling garlic-parsley butter.

dishes.name: Croque monsieur
dishes.what: Toasted ham-and-cheese sandwich topped with béchamel; with a fried egg it's a croque madame.

dishes.name: Quiche Lorraine
dishes.what: Savoury open tart filled with egg custard and bacon.

dishes.name: Crème brûlée
dishes.what: Vanilla custard with a crackly layer of burnt sugar on top.

dishes.name: Macaron
dishes.what: Pastel sandwich biscuits of almond meringue with a creamy filling.
